In the Fanny May mill, the sample is preheated under aluminum blocks in an oven until temperature equilibration. Lamination of the ASL + ASL/AFL/GDC has not been evaluated in this work, but is expected to behave similarly due to the identical composition of the ASL layers. The microstructure of the individual layer by layer laminate was evaluated with SEM (Configuration 1 on right) and revealed a cohesive EEA with no delamination between the interface of various layers. A very tight interface is seen with the dense structure of the EEA layers tightly bound to each other. 15 The main finding was that limiting the amount of passes in the calender results in less damage to the EEA, and while configuration 1 may show good interface contact, configuration 2 resulted in a laminate stack without any surface damage. Surface imperfections may be resolved in the binder burn out stage under high temperature firing, and this will be investigated, however, the conclusions drawn in this report period indicate that the optimal manufacturing conditions in terms of EEA quality, may be layer by layer deposition via slot-die coating to form the ASL/ASL/AFL and lamination of the GDC electrolyte to form the EEA stack, in one pass through the calender at elevated temperature. After determination of appropriate speed and force conditions on the Fenn May Mill in the 4-High configuration, the screening of processing temperature proceeded at three levels, 16 90°C, 110°C and 130°C, for calendering of the EEA in various configurations, including: lamination layer-by-layer, 2-layer/2-layer and 3-layer/1-layer. Previous efforts included the processing window at these temperatures as well as room temperature on the BMF’s heated calender. As an alternative to this equipment which is unavailable due to maintenance, we implemented a 2-stage process, with samples preheated at the set temperature until equilibration in a convection oven, followed by lamination at 25 FPM (feet per minute) and 16,000 pounds of separating force on the Fenn 4-High mill. The residence time of the sample heat treatment was 5 minutes, with the desired temperature checked to be at equilibrium with a temperature reader. The lamination configurations for the SOFC EEA stack (ASL/ASL/AFL/GDC) fabrication proceeded via the following configurations: 1) single-layer buildup: ASL+ASL  ASL/ASL + AFL  ASL/ASL/AFL + GDC, and multiple-layer coatings laminated together: 2) ASL/ASL + AFL  ASL/ASL/AFL + GDC, 3) ASL/ASL + AFL/GDC and 4) ASL/ASL/AFL + GDC.
